statement.excerpt: Mollick’s notion of “jagged” AI is exactly what I used to mean by the term “pointillisitic” and what I predicted about o3 in November. AI that works some of the time but not always, markedly better on some problems than others.
statement.document_title: OpenAI’s o3 and Tyler Cowen’s Misguided AGI Fantasy

our_interpretation: The plain performance claim is that launch-era o3 combines substantial strengths with important task-dependent weaknesses.
Works some of the time does not specify an overall success percentage or mean that most answers fail.
The November attribution is a separate factual component requiring a dated contemporaneous record; November is read as November 2024.
The target period covers the ongoing performance observation at release. Earlier prediction records are treated as historical context and checked separately.
This is an observation plus a retrospective attribution, not a new forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Launch-era evaluations establish pronounced strengths and weaknesses, and a contemporaneous November 2024 record establishes the attributed prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations undermine the asserted unevenness, or a sufficiently complete historical record establishes that the November attribution is wrong. Finding a later prediction alone does not prove none existed earlier.

evidence.explanation: The launch disclosure documents strong coding and multimodal performance. Together with the system card's factual-answer failures, it supports the performance component of the claim.

The accompanying table reports o3 accuracy of 0.49 on SimpleQA and 0.59 on PersonQA, with substantial hallucination rates. These documented weaknesses coexist with its strong benchmark results; they do not provide a universal everyday-use accuracy rate.
